correctness.rationale: For the monomial preimage \(f_{a,n}(z)=z+a z^n\), the transformed logarithmic derivative reduces exactly to a Möbius function of \(w=\Omega_n a z^{n-1}\). Its sharp disk supremum gives membership iff \(|a|\le \delta/[\Omega_n(n-1+\delta)]\). The original derivative has an interior zero iff \(|a|>1/n\), and the positive-real-part calculation gives the identical exact starlikeness threshold. Comparing the thresholds yields \(\delta_n=\Omega_n(n-1)/(n-\Omega_n)\); the explicit multiplier formula gives \(\delta_n\sim\Omega_n\to0\).

value.rationale: The source construction naturally raises whether shrinking the transformed disk target can force geometry back onto the original preimage. The exact mode threshold \(\delta_n=\Omega_n(n-1)/(n-\Omega_n)\) gives a complete answer on every single-mode slice and shows \(\delta_n\to0\). Therefore no positive uniform inverse-preservation radius exists on the full class. This is a structural obstruction, not a routine coefficient substitution, and it identifies what any future positive theorem must overcome.
